clue.text: Some rice left in taxi. What language!

indicators.note: the rice fragment is left inside the cab, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a taxi is a cab
some of the word rice: its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone spills rice in a cab, and the driver swears colourfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What language!' looks like an exclamation at bad words, but it is the definition: a language of the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Carib is the tongue of an indigenous people of the Lesser Antilles and northern South America.

clue.text: Partner shows Clubs following a pass

indicators.note: the clubs come after the pass, so that piece goes second

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a league is a group of clubs

explanation.surface: A bridge partner shows the club suit after a pass.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a bridge auction: a pass, then a bid in clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague is an associate or fellow worker, a partner in work.

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of heron running riot into a new order

explanation.surface: An untamed wading bird flies across the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river flows through Switzerland and France, a waterway running across the continent.

clue.text: Domed structure at end of direct flight line

definitions.text: Domed structure at end of direct flight line

parts.words: Domed structure at end of direct flight line
parts.note: insects fly straight home along a bee-line, which ends at their domed home

explanation.surface: An airport terminal with a dome where a nonstop air route ends.
explanation.walkthrough: A bee-line is the straightest route; a bee heading home flies one straight to its skep.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional straw skep is dome-shaped, and is where a bee flying straight home arrives.

indicators.note: the stone and the layers swap places, so the clue's order is turned round in the grid

parts.note: geological layers are strata
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A gadget for shifting layers of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a scheme or trick, a device in the sense of a ploy.

definitions.meaning: a heavy smith's hammer, as in sledgehammer
Santa Claus rides through the sky on a sleigh

explanation.surface: Asking about the hammer belonging to Saint Nicholas.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy two-handed hammer is so called, and Father Christmas travels in a sleigh of that name.

clue.text: Made better by right to a new freedom

indicators.note: new tells you to make a fresh arrangement of the letters of freedom

explanation.surface: A society improved by giving people the right to a new kind of liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reformed has been improved, changed for the better.

definitions.meaning: a politician who shifts with the times to stay in favour

explanation.surface: A hairdresser who goes into politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdresser clips hair; politically, a time-server changes sides for advantage.

parts.note: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote an opera about Venetian rowers, who stand at the back of their craft

explanation.surface: A severe ferryman created by W S Gilbert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' seems to mean strict, but the Venetian oarsman stands in the stern of his boat; Gilbert wrote the libretto of The Gondoliers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian boatman propels his craft standing at its stern, and gave a Savoy opera its title.

definitions.meaning: an old name for the walrus, with possessive 's acting as 'is'
the telegraphic code of dots and dashes

explanation.surface: The way a sea creature talks to others.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for the walrus is also the dot-and-dash telegraph code.

clue.text: Sort of book that tends to fall off in autumn

definitions.text: that tends to fall off in autumn

explanation.surface: A kind of book whose pages drop out as the year turns.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: a leaf on a tree that is loose drops off in autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A binder with removable pages is this kind of book; a detached tree leaf falls in the autumn.

clue.text: Marksman's second best sort of tube

definitions.meaning: on a shooting target the ring next to the bull scores second highest
the rubber tube inside a tyre

explanation.surface: A shooter's runner-up score turns out to be a kind of tube.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring just outside the bull on a target is so called, as is the inflatable tube within a tyre.

parts.note: reads like a shop opening late being a blunder, but describes a flower whose blooms unfold at dusk

explanation.surface: Someone groans at a business that opened late: what a mistake!
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow-flowered plant opens its blossoms towards nightfall, so it is a bloomer that opens late.

definitions.meaning: a North American rodent that digs tunnels
the biblical timber from which Noah built the ark

explanation.surface: An animal that digs its home in the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocket rodent of North America shares its name with the ark's timber in Genesis.

indicators.note: a concoction mixes ingredients, so the letters of beer and crisp are blended

explanation.surface: A pub suggests a drink and a packet of crisps together.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who prescribes a remedy advises it, recommending a course of treatment.

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, a large number
earning, being paid for work

explanation.surface: Lots of people labouring in order to understand things.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is acquired scholarship, the knowledge gained by study.

clue.text: Supplier of current information-the muse? Right

parts.note: gen is informal British for information
Erato is the Greek muse of lyric poetry

explanation.surface: A source of up-to-date news asks whether the muse is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'up-to-date' but means electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo produces electricity, so it supplies electric current.

clue.text: In rude upbringing it's Felix Love who taught us

indicators.note: the cat and love sit in the reversed word, contained within it
in a down clue, bringing up a word reverses it upwards

parts.note: Felix is a famous cartoon cat
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A teacher recalls a coarse childhood with a cat called Felix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upbringing' reverses RUDE to EDUR, and 'In' puts CAT and O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher or schoolmaster is someone who instructed us.

clue.text: Happening to die, sadly, in time for 11

parts.note: an event is something that happens

indicators.note: the word die is upset, sadly scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: An event leads to someone dying, a sad occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' turns DIE into IDE. 11 is EVENING PRIMROSE, which flowers at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is the poetic word for evening, when that flower opens.

indicators.note: ruin wrecks the word so its letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: the word with its possessive s kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A bottle of gin, the drink nicknamed mother's ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: Mother's ruin is British slang for gin.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum flask keeps drinks hot or cold; the brand name became generic.

definitions.meaning: ... Hastings, first Governor-General of British India: this is his first name

explanation.surface: A secret tunnel system belonging to the town of Hastings.
explanation.definitionFit: The governor's forename doubles as a maze of rabbit burrows below ground.

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on top of another comes first

parts.note: an ace is an expert
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: An art gallery has an expert in salt.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetate is a salt or ester of acetic acid, a chemical compound of that kind.

definitions.meaning: metal fastenings, or bars on a medal ribbon

explanation.surface: Pubs that hug their customers.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastening bars and buckles are so called, and the verb means hugs or grips.

parts.note: a driver parking illegally collects a fine, while at a railway station staff collect fares

explanation.surface: A car left on a yellow line spotted near the London station.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo is a major London railway terminus where barrier staff check tickets; an illegal parker also gathers parking tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway official checking passes at a station, and jokingly a motorist who accumulates fines.

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: An ancient village where a loud man sits at the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorp is an archaic word for a hamlet, surviving in English place names.

definitions.meaning: the Hebridean island of Harris is famed for its woollen cloth

explanation.surface: A plant grown on the island of Harris.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower means a thing that flows: the River Tweed on the Scottish border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Border river and the rough woollen cloth woven on the Scottish isle share a name.

parts.note: the den in question is named after the drug smoked in pipes there

explanation.surface: A lair where people sit puffing on pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: The narcotic from poppies gave its name to dens where it was smoked in pipes.

parts.note: a test is a trial

indicators.note: the word meant is changing its letter order

explanation.surface: A court hearing meant a witness changed their story.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is evidence or proof, something bearing witness to a fact.

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Tam o' Shanter: the missing word is the delights that soon fade

explanation.surface: A line of Robert Burns with one word gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns continues 'You seize the flow'r, its bloom is shed': joys vanish as quickly as a picked poppy.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank in Burns's line is filled by the word for delights or enjoyments.

definitions.meaning: a lay officer in Presbyterian and other churches
a small tree with white flowers and dark berries

explanation.surface: A clergyman spotted out in the park.
explanation.definitionFit: A Presbyterian lay official shares a name with the sambucus tree growing in parks.
